_readme: Verified 'these different NAMES are one company' facts.
insurer_key() in canonicalize_financials.py collapses TYPOGRAPHIC variants only
- case, '&' vs 'and', 'Co. Ltd.' vs 'Ltd', punctuation. It deliberately does not
strip distinguishing words, because doing so would fuse separately licensed
entities of one group: Bajaj Allianz Life and Bajaj Allianz General are two
That leaves a gap no string function can close. When the handbook renders one
company under two genuinely different names, only a real-world fact can merge
them. This file is where those facts live, so the default stays conservative and
every merge is explicit, reviewable and attributable.
Add an entry ONLY after confirming the companies are the same legal entity.
A wrong entry here silently fuses two real insurers into one, which is far
harder to notice than the split it fixes.
'canonical' is pinned as the display name - it overrides the usual
longest-variant heuristic, which would otherwise have picked the wrong Galaxy
name simply because it is longer.

variants: Galaxy Health and Allied Insurance Ltd.
why: One SAHI insurer appearing under two names in different tables of
handbook_2024-25_parts.xlsx. Evidence: identical insurer class (SAHI),
same source workbook, and ZERO overlapping (metric, line-of-business,
year) triples - the two names carry complementary halves of one book,
not duplicate filings. 'Galaxy Health and Allied Insurance Ltd.' held
8 lines of business (Health, Balance Sheet, Investments, Claims);
'Galaxy Health Insurance Co. Ltd' held Personal Accident alone,
stranding 6,390 policies and 274 lakh of gross premium off the profile.
Confirmed as the same company by the user on 2026-07-30, who also
chose the 'Co. Ltd' rendering as canonical.

DIVERGES DELIBERATELY from the Annual Report, which prints the older 'and Allied' form in both Annexure 1 (p.157) and Annexure 7 (p.172). The company's own website now uses 'Galaxy Health Insurance Co. Ltd', i.e. it dropped 'and Allied' after the report was published. Confirmed by the user on 2026-07-30. The 'and Allied' form stays in variants, so registry matching and anyone searching the old name still hit.
The handbook writes this insurer as the bare abbreviation 'CAL', so no
re-extraction can recover the name - it is not in the source.
Confirmed from IRDAI Annual Report 2024-25, Annexure 7 (Number of Products &
Riders, page 172), which lists 'CreditAccess Life Insurance Ltd..' at S.No 10
of the Life insurers, Private Sector.
Corroborated by the data: CAL appears in exactly two handbook tables,
'Micro-Insurance Death Claims - Group' and 'Micro-Insurance Claim Settlement -
Group', for 2023-24 and 2024-25 only. Of the 24 filers in those tables, 23 are
named '...Life...' and CAL is the sole exception - they are the life insurers'
group micro-insurance statements.
Renaming also fixes the CLASS: insurer_class is derived from the name after
aliases are applied, so 'CAL' (which matched nothing) was falling through to
General while sitting in a life-only table.

insurer_class is pinned here rather than left to the name-based derivation, because that derivation is skipped whenever the DB already carries the column - so a stored 'General' would survive the rename.

A third rendering, 'Credit Access Life Insurance Ltd.' (356 rows), was found reconciling against the Annual Report - so this insurer was split THREE ways: 'CAL', 'CreditAccess' and 'Credit Access'. Zero overlapping (metric, lob, fy) triples across all three. Annexure 6 (p.171, S.No 11) prints it closed up as 'CreditAccess Life Insurance Ltd.'
'Aegas' is a misspelling of 'Ageas' in the handbook - the letters are transposed.
Same class (Life), zero overlapping (metric, lob, fy) triples, 1,150 rows stranded off
the 2,008-row main book. Annual Report 2024-25 Annexure 7 (p.172, S.No 4 of Life,
Private Sector) prints 'Ageas Federal Life Insurance Co. Ltd.', confirming the spelling.
Canonical keeps our dominant existing rendering so the insurer_id does not churn.

aliases.canonical: Future Generali India Insurance Co. Ltd.
variants: Future Generali India Insurance Co. Ltd.
Future Generali India Insurance C. Ltd.
why: 'C. Ltd.' is a typo for 'Co. Ltd.'. Both are the GENERAL insurer - the life business is a
separate entity (future_generali_india_life_insurance_ltd) and is untouched here.
The main general book (1,644 rows, 17 lines of business) was split from a
Personal-Accident-only fragment (397 rows), with zero overlapping triples.
Confirmed present as one general insurer in Annexure 3 (p.162, S.No 4, printed
'Future Generalli General Insurance Co. Ltd.' - the report's own typo).
NOTE: renamed to Generali Central Insurance after this report; the display name is
left as filed for now so it matches the handbook and the Annual Report.

aliases.canonical: Zurich Kotak General Insurance Co. (India) Ltd.
variants: Zurich Kotak General Insurance Co. (India) Ltd.
Kotak Mahindra General Insurance Co. Ltd.
why: IRDAI Annual Report 2024-25, Annexure 1 (p.157) lists this insurer as 'Zurich Kotak General Insurance Co. (India) Ltd.'
with '(erstwhile Kotak Mahindra General Ins. Co. Ltd.)' printed beside it.
Unlike the other renames, our data holds BOTH names as separate entities -
929 rows under the old, 991 under the new, with zero overlapping
(metric, lob, fy) triples - so this is a merge, not just a display change.

variants: General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re)
why: IRDAI Annual Report 2024-25, Annexure 1 (p.158) lists the public-sector reinsurer as 'General Insurance Corporation of India'.
Our data appends '(GIC Re)'. Same entity; the suffix is a market nickname.

The handbook uses a market short name where the report uses the full legal one. Token matching cannot bridge these - 'Munich' is not a substring of 'Munchener', and 'Re' is not 'Reinsurance' - so the mapping is declared rather than inferred. Canonical is the report's form so registry matching succeeds; the short name stays in variants so it remains searchable.

variants: Lloyd's of India - Markel Services Private Limited
why: One Lloyd's service company written two ways in the handbook - once standalone
as 'Markel Services P Ltd.' and once as a Lloyd's sub-entry - which made the FRB
count read 13 against the official 12.
IRDAI Annual Report 2024-25 Annexure 1 (p.158) lists it once, at S.No 11 of
Service Companies of Lloyd's, as 'Markel Services India Private Limited'.
Note it was ALSO classified General in our data while being a Lloyd's service
company, which is why it appeared in the general-insurer picker.
